title: Days, months and dates
goal: By the end of this lesson you can name the days and months, say and write dates the French way (le 24 juin), talk about habits (le lundi) and plans (lundi), and use the Quebec word for weekend: la fin de semaine.

body: The days are masculine and written with a lowercase letter: *lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche*. The French week starts on Monday.
Without an article, a day means one specific day: *Je travaille lundi* (I'm working this Monday). With *le*, it means every week: *Je travaille le lundi* (I work on Mondays).
learn.tip: lundi = this Monday; le lundi = every Monday.

body: Months are also masculine and lowercase: *janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre*.
Use *en* or *au mois de* for 'in': *en janvier, au mois d'août*. *Août* is pronounced [oot] (most Quebecers) or [oo].
French dates use *le* + number + month: *le 24 juin*, *le 15 mars 2026*. Use ordinary numbers (*le deux, le trois*), except for the first day of the month: *le premier* (1er).
To ask the date: *Quelle est la date aujourd'hui?* or casually *On est le combien aujourd'hui?* Answer: *On est le 3 mai* or *C'est le 3 mai*. With a day: *On est lundi, le 3 mai*.
In Quebec, numeric dates are often written year-month-day (2026-05-03), as recommended by the OQLF. When in doubt, write the month in words.

body: Useful words around dates: *aujourd'hui* (today), *demain* (tomorrow), *hier* (yesterday), *la semaine* (week), *le mois* (month), *l'année* / *l'an* (year).
Add *prochain* (next) or *dernier* (last) after the noun: *lundi prochain*, *la semaine prochaine*, *le mois dernier*. In Quebec, *passé* is also very common: *la semaine passée*, *dimanche passé*.

In Quebec, the weekend is *la fin de semaine* (literally 'end of week'). The English-looking *le week-end*, normal in France, is understood but much less used. *Bonne fin de semaine!* is what everyone says on Friday.

Two key Quebec dates: *le 24 juin* is the Fête nationale (also called *la Saint-Jean*), and *le 1er juillet* is Canada Day, but also Quebec's moving day (*le jour du déménagement*), when many leases end.
